deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 35–37): Grothendieck is classifying the special loci of M_{0,5}, i.e. 5-point configurations K on a Riemann sphere Σ with extra symmetry. Page 35 treated antiholomorphic involutions (real structures). The adjacent page that sets up this one treats a holomorphic involution u. In that case u has exactly one fixed point P = ∞ in K, and it swaps the other four points I in two pairs. Logically that adjacent page precedes this one.

Setup. Let 0 be the other fixed point of u. Then T_1 = Σ∖{0,∞} is a C*-torsor, i.e. T_1 = L_1^* for a complex line L_1, and u acts as multiplication by −1. The set I is a pair of {±1}-orbits {±a} and {±b}. Squaring gives two distinct points ξ = a², η = b² of T_2 = L_2^*, where L_2 = L_1^{⊗2}. Their product e = ξη lies in T_4 = L_1^{⊗4} minus 0.

This page.
(1) The invariant is λ = (ξ+η)²/(ξ∧η) = ξ/η + η/ξ + 2. It is unchanged by rescaling T_1 and by swapping ξ and η. It determines the configuration up to isomorphism. The only condition on λ is λ ≠ 4, which is equivalent to ξ ≠ η. So this stratum is the λ-line minus one point, a complex curve.
(2) Choose a basis e_1 of L_1 with e_1^{⊗4} = e. Writing ξ = ξ_0 e_1², η = η_0 e_1² gives ξ_0 η_0 = 1. The data then reduce to μ = ξ_0 + η_0 with μ ≠ ±2, and λ = μ². The numbers ξ_0, η_0 are the roots of z² − μz + 1 = 0. They are distinct exactly when μ ≠ ±2, and automatically nonzero since their product is 1.
(3) The four points I are the roots of z⁴ − μz² + 1 = 0, namely I = {±√((μ ± √(μ²−4))/2)} = {±√(μ' ± √(μ'²−1))} with μ' = μ/2.

Purpose: an explicit normal form for the one-dimensional fixed locus in M_{0,5} of an involution of type (ab)(cd) in S_5. This feeds the census of special real and complex strata of M_{0,5} (cf. the counts on p. 35, e.g. 15 components). That census belongs to Grothendieck's 1983–84 study of the Teichmüller tower and its 'Lego' of low-dimensional moduli spaces.
errors: No mathematical error. The algebra is correct: λ = μ², the roots of z⁴ − μz² + 1 are as stated, and μ' = μ/2 gives the second form.

Minor gap: the phrase 'à iso unique près' should read 'up to isomorphism'. Every such configuration has u itself as a nontrivial automorphism. At λ = μ = 0 (I = the 4th roots of unity, the 'pyramidal carré' configuration) there is an extra automorphism z ↦ iz, so the λ-line is a coarse moduli space with a stacky point at λ = 0. The page does not remark on this.
The rigidification is only defined up to sign: e_1 is defined up to μ_4, so μ is defined only up to sign. This is consistent with λ = μ² being the true invariant, but it is implicit.

ideas.what: Parametrize 5-point configurations on P^1 with a holomorphic involution (fixing one marked point) by the invariant λ = ξ/η + η/ξ + 2, using the C*-torsor and tensor-power language (T_1, T_2 = T^{∧2}, T_4, reduction of structure group to μ_4).
ideas.modern_name: fixed locus of an S_5 involution on M_{0,5}; normal form of symmetric configurations
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (folklore on symmetric point configurations and automorphisms of M_{0,n})
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,5} and its special points/curves in general terms; this explicit computation is not published as far as known

ideas.what: Normal form z⁴ − μz² + 1 = 0 for the four exchanged points, with μ ≠ ±2.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine explicit computation of a well-known one-dimensional symmetric stratum of M_{0,5}. Its only interest is as a piece of Grothendieck's systematic census of special strata of M_{0,5}, which is documented elsewhere in spirit.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: read 'à iso unique près' instead of 'i.e. [-nous-] unique près'.
'La condition vraie sur λ' should probably read 'La condition unique sur λ'.
'e_1^{⊗2} = e' should be e_1^{⊗4} = e (the superscript in the image is 4; e lies in T_4 = L_1^{⊗4}).
The leading 'le carré est' refers to μ² = λ: λ is the square of the quantity μ introduced below.
